Appellants/claimants have filed this appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 being aggrieved by award dated 12/9/2014 passed by First Ad d itio nal Motor Accident claims Tribunal,
Gwalior in Claim Case No.131/2013; whereby, the Claims Tribunal has awarded a compensation of Rs. 5,51,000/- alongwith interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum to the claimants/respondents No. 1 to 6.

sentences.text: The liability for payment of compensation amount was fixed on appellant/Insurance Company and respondents No. 7 and 8 jointly and severally.

2. Briefly stated facts of the case are that claimants filed a claim case stated that deceased Bhupendra Yadav was a young youth of 28 years and engaged in labour works and thereby used to ear Rs. 6,000/- per month.
Deceased was son of respondents No. 1 and 2 and brother of respondents No. 3 to 6.

It was alleged that when deceased was going on foot to seek Darshan of Munde wale Baba, at about 6.30 am, the driver of offending vehicle Bolero bearing registration No.
MP07BA0225, by driving it in a very rash and negligent manner, dashed the deceased, due to which he sustained grievous hurts and succumbed to the same on the spot.
Therefore, claimants filed claim petition, which stood partly allowed by impugned award.
Therefore, Insurance Company is before this Court, assailing the liability part of the impugned award.

3. It is the submission of learned counsel for the appellant/Insurance Company that as per FIR and Final report, deceased was sitting in the bolero as a passenger; however, the Claims Tribunal gave finding that deceased was on foot while offending vehicle dashed him and since deceased was travelling as passenger in the Bolero, the Insurance Company was not liable to be fastened with the liability as the vehicle was being run against the terms and condition of the policy.
4.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondents supported the impugned award and prayed for dismissal of the appeal.

Respondents no. 1 to 6 also filed cross-objections vide I.A.No.
500/2015 for enhancement of the compensation amount.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties at length and perused the record.
6.
Appeal is filed by the Insurance Company on the ground of non- liability.

As regards cross Cross objections filed by the claimants/respondents No. 1 to 6 for enhancement;
but no Court fees paid.
Otherwise also in the opinion of this Court, the findings as regards earning and dependency recorded by the Claims Tribunal are proper and the amount of award is also proper.
Cross objections rejected.
I.A.No. 500/2015 is accordingly dismissed.
8. It is not in dispute that the respondent No.7 has caused the death of deceased Bhupendra Yadav by negligently driving the vehicle Bolero bearing Registration No.M.P.07BA-0225.

It is also an admitted fact that this vehicle was insured with appellant Insurance Company on the date of accident and the policy is only act-policy and under the policy neither the risk of occupants of vehicle is covered nor any premium has been paid by the owner for this purpose.
9. It is contended by the claimants that at the time of accident the deceased Bhupendra was going on foot and the vehicle in question hit him from behind.
In this regard two witnesses Ramavtar and Harcharan Singh Yadav who are said to the eye witnesses of the accident have been examined.
But their testimony is full of contradictions and does not inspire confidence and their presence on the spot at the time of accident is doubtful.
No one has lodged any report with the police stating the facts mentioned in their statements.
Witness Harcharan has lodge marg report in the concerned Police Station Murar.
In this report also he has not disclosed the fact of occurrence of accident before him.
But as per this report he has reached the spot later on and has seen the dead body of the deceased.
Moreover, the conduct of these witnesses who hail from the same community and village as that of the claimants is also unnatural and doubtful.
10. As per the police report which has been lodged after marg enquiry and the chargesheet papers the deceased was travelling in the vehicle in question at the time of accident.
The statement of witness Harcharan in the Tribunal is also contrary to the police statement (Ex.D/1) and other police papers containing his signature.

It is true that the statements recorded in the Tribunal should be given weightage over police papers and FIR is not a substantive piece of evidence and it can be used for corroboration and contradiction of its maker as has been held by Apex Court in the matter of Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Premlata Shukla and Ors., 2007ACJ1928(SC).

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Premlata Shukla and Ors., 2007ACJ1928(SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But, they should be without any infirmity but the veracity and the reliability of such statements can be checked in the context of their previous statements.
There is no reason for the police to prepare false papers and change the nature of the accident.
No complaint of any sort has been made against the concerned police officer by the claimants or by the witnesses.
It is also apposite to mention that the claimants have themselves relied upon the police papers for proving the accident.
Beside it, the nature of injuries as mentioned in the post morterm report (Ex. P/7) caused to the deceased in the accident also does not support the version of the claimants and their witnesses.
These injuries are not possible to be cause by hitting the vehicle from behind.
The fact of the dead-body lying outside the vehicle also does not alone prove the above version.
The Investigation Officer Surendra Singh Somwanshi (DW/2) has clearly stated the fact of taking out of the dead-body from the vehicle by the villagers and lying of blood in the vehicle.
There is no reason for discarding his testimony.
The statement given by the driver of the vehicle in the Tribunal regarding going in the vehicle all alone is not in conformity with written statement filed by him in the Tribunal.
His statement is in support of the claimants is meant only to avoid his liability.
Hence it is not worthy of credence.
The circumstances surrounding the accident also do not support the claimants.

sentences.text: Thus, it is clear from police papers itself that their version remained the same from beginning to end and there are major contradictions in the statement of witnesses tried to be projected as eye witnesses.

Thus, in the light of decision of Madras High Court in the matter of New India Assurance Co. Ltd. vs. S.Krishnasamy and Ors., 2016(2)TAC125(Mad.),
deceased being only occupant of private car, cannot be considered as third party of vehicle and since policy covers risk to the third party alone, policy will not cover the risk of deceased and therefore,
Insurance Company cannot be held liable for payment of compensation amount and further since deceased was not a third party, in such matter doctrine of pay and recover cannot be applied and owner of the vehicle alone is liable to pay damages to the claimants, as accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the vehicle.

11. In the result, appeal is allowed to the extent indicated hereinabove and impugned award is also modified to that extent.
